pr_body:
We just avoid the special handling needed for Apple M1.

Fixes #26135
pr_comments: Don't we need to work around the same issue on arm64_32?

> Don't we need to work around the same issue on arm64_32?

You mean the original one that was fixed by this arch-specific hack? I do not think so. It was not reproducible on hardware, only on VMs.
A VM also needs to work correctly.

> A VM also needs to work correctly.

But is there any VM with that platform? AFAIK not. Besides even if there was we would not know if it is affected by the same issue.

> > A VM also needs to work correctly.
> 
> But is there any VM with that platform? 

No other Apple products uses `arm64_32` so its safe to assume that there's no watchOS simulators built for `arm64_32`.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.4 an 3.3 branches. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: OpenSSL 3.4.0 crashes on arm64_32 devices (for example, Apple Watch)
comments: How can the arm64_32 architecture be distinguished from a regular aarch64 build?
Is there something like `__aarch64_32__` defined on this platform?

Looking at https://reviews.llvm.org/D63131#change-RyFMReTm1DPr it appears possible that `__ARM64_ARCH_8_32__` might be defined (otherwise it's some horrible combination of `__APPLE__ && __aarch64__ && !__LP64__`), but I'm not set up to test this
@t8m, based on the example project, utilising  #26145 works fine on my Apple Watch.
